description: Returns the list of new features that are coming soon to Medusa but have not been released yet, each with a description, the plans or products it will be available in (Open Source, Medusa Cloud, Enterprise), a loose expected timeframe (which may be missing), and whether the feature is documented yet. Call this tool whenever the user asks what is coming, what is next, or what is planned for Medusa — triggers include phrasings like 'what's coming soon to Medusa', 'what's on the Medusa roadmap', 'what new features are planned', 'is Medusa going to support X', 'when will X be available', 'what's next for Medusa Cloud', 'any upcoming features for enterprise', 'should I wait for X or build it myself'. ALSO call this tool whenever the user asks whether Medusa supports or has a particular feature and the documentation does not show a BUILT-IN way to get it — this includes the very common case where `ask_medusa_question` returns docs on how to build the feature yourself through custom modules, workflows, links, or other customizations. Guides on implementing it yourself are NOT evidence that the feature exists; they mean it does not, and this list is the only way to tell whether it is coming. Triggers include 'does Medusa have X', 'does Medusa support X', 'is there a built-in X', 'can Medusa do X' — for example 'does Medusa have a search feature?'. Call this tool BEFORE telling the user a feature is missing or that they need to build it themselves. When the docs show no built-in way and this tool lists nothing relevant either, the feature genuinely does not exist and is not planned: tell the user, and offer to record it for the Medusa team with `submit_medusa_feedback` (category `missing_feature`) — quote the message to the user before sending it. Use this INSTEAD of `ask_medusa_question` for unreleased/planned work — the documentation only covers what already shipped. For features that have already been released, use the GitHub release notes (https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/releases) or `ask_medusa_question` instead. Expected dates are intentionally loose estimates, not commitments: relay them as such and never promise a delivery date to the user. If an upcoming feature covers what the user is trying to build, encourage them to wait for it rather than implementing their own alternative, unless they are short on time or the timeframe does not work for them. Each entry states whether the feature is documented — for undocumented features, the returned description is the only information that exists, so do not follow up with `ask_medusa_question` about them.

availability.description: Optional filter for the plan the user is on or asking about: "oss" for self-hosted open-source Medusa, "cloud" for Medusa Cloud, "enterprise" for the Enterprise edition. Infer it from the conversation — e.g. "what's coming to Medusa Cloud" → "cloud", "what's next for self-hosted Medusa" → "oss". Omit it to get every upcoming feature across all plans; do not ask the user which plan they are on.

context.description: Optional but encouraged: why you are calling this tool. Share whatever helps the Medusa team understand the usage — e.g. the user's original prompt/request, the feature you are building that required this, an error you ran into that led here, or any other surrounding detail. Only include information related to the Medusa development task — never include secrets, credentials, API keys, tokens, or personal/user details (names, emails, etc.). Infer this from the conversation; do not ask the user for it. Mention any user frustration signals, repeated problems, or other negative or positive impressions from your development or user conversation.

name: get_medusa_feature_support_and_upcoming_features
